name: Product Spec (PM-led PRD)
description: A product manager writes a detailed, build-ready PRD — fed by parallel user research and an engineering feasibility read, then sharpened by a sprint-scoping pass. Use this when you already know you want the thing and need the spec engineers can build against. Fan-in on the PM, then a scoping refinement. Optional arena mode (PS-3, behind orchestration.arena.enabled) runs parallel candidates across distinct model families (Claude + Gemini) on the PRD step, cross-judged and synthesized. Other candidate steps for arena: product-brief (synthesis), idea-to-launch (prd), gtm-campaign (offer/core message). Never use arena for media renders or operations. All roles pinned to product/engineering agents; brain chains remain editable in the UI.

steps.title: User & problem research: {{idea}}
steps.description: Research the users and the real problem behind "{{idea}}": who has this problem, how they solve it today, the top 3 unmet needs, and the 5-8 concrete user stories that matter most. Cite evidence or clearly mark assumptions. Output as markdown.
acceptance: user-research.md is saved in the artifacts dir naming the target user segment(s) and how they solve the problem today
5-8 user stories in 'As a <user>, I want <x> so that <y>' form
Every claim cites a source URL or is marked ASSUMPTION

steps.title: Engineering feasibility read: {{idea}}
steps.description: Give a fast engineering feasibility read on "{{idea}}": the core components, the hardest technical risk, external dependencies/APIs required, a rough effort tier (S/M/L) per component, and anything that would materially change scope. Output as markdown.
acceptance: feasibility.md is saved in the artifacts dir listing core components, each with an S/M/L effort tier
The single hardest technical risk is named with a mitigation
External dependencies/APIs are listed by name (or 'none')

steps.title: Write the PRD: {{idea}}
steps.description: You are the Product Manager. Using the user research and the engineering feasibility read provided, write the detailed PRD for "{{idea}}": problem statement, target users & prioritized user stories, MVP scope with an explicit OUT-of-scope list, functional + non-functional requirements, success metrics & instrumentation, key edge cases, dependencies, and open questions with owners. Be diplomatically ruthless about focus. Output the full PRD as markdown.
acceptance: prd.md is saved in the artifacts dir with sections: problem, users & stories, MVP scope, out of scope, functional & non-functional requirements, success metrics, edge cases, dependencies, open questions
Every open question has an owner
Each success metric names how it is instrumented
MVP stories trace to the user-research stories
verify: test -s prd.md && grep -ciE '^#+ .*(problem|scope|out of scope|requirement|metric|edge|dependenc|open question)' prd.md  # >= 8

rubric: Completeness: covers problem, users, stories, MVP scope, out-of-scope, functional/non-functional requirements, metrics, edge cases
Traceability: every user story traces to user research and every metric names its instrumentation
Boundary discipline: ruthless cut list and clear out-of-scope boundaries
Actionability: engineering can build directly from requirements and edge cases without guessing

steps.title: Scope into a shippable first sprint: {{idea}}
steps.description: Take the PRD provided and cut it into a shippable first sprint for "{{idea}}": the smallest slice that delivers real user value, an ordered backlog of tickets each with a one-line acceptance criterion, the explicit cut list (what's deferred and why), and the top risk to the sprint. Output as markdown.
acceptance: sprint.md is saved in the artifacts dir with an ordered backlog where every ticket has a one-line acceptance criterion
An explicit cut list says what is deferred and why
The top sprint risk is named
Every ticket traces to an MVP item in the PRD
verify: every backlog ticket line in sprint.md has an acceptance criterion
